note: Stored routing policy for the headscale subnet router on this host.
This is deliberately NARROWER than cockpit-wireguard's routing-policy.json,
because headscale already owns most of what that file has to declare:
- WHICH prefixes may be routed is decided by route approval, held in
headscale's database and declared in acl-policy.hujson autoApprovers.
- The FORWARD/MASQUERADE rules for approved subnets are programmed by
tailscaled into its own ts-* chains. Do not write those rules here.
What is left is the host state tailscaled does NOT manage and that nothing
restores if it disappears:
1. Forwarding sysctls. tailscaled WARNS when ip_forward is off and then
carries on; it never sets or re-asserts them. An exit node advertising
::/0 with IPv6 forwarding off fails only for v6, which presents as
'some sites hang', not as an outage.
2. The jump from the built-in FORWARD chain into ts-forward, and its
ORDER. A podman/libvirt/docker restart or any iptables-restore strips
the jump; the ts-* chains survive intact and are simply never reached.
Worse, if LIBVIRT_FWI ends up ahead of ts-forward, the libvirt networks
(172.20.10.0/24 and 192.168.122.0/24) are REJECTed for tailnet clients
while every other route keeps working.
3. The advertised set itself. `tailscale up` is NOT additive: a later bare
`tailscale up` drops --advertise-routes and --advertise-exit-node, and
the node silently stops serving while still showing online.
Keep advertise_routes in step with acl-policy.hujson autoApprovers.routes -
a prefix advertised but not auto-approved needs a manual approve-routes call,
and that call REPLACES the node's whole approved set.

router.note: accept_dns is false on purpose: edt1 runs its own resolver, and letting the tailnet push MagicDNS over the host would hijack DNS for every service on it.
